answer_text:
We need \(Z = \mathbb{E}(X|\mathcal{G})\), meaning \(Z\) is \(\mathcal{G}\)-measurable and

\[
\int_A Z\,d\lambda=\int_A X\,d\lambda
\qquad \text{for all } A\in\mathcal{G}.
\]

Here \(\mathcal{G}\) consists of countable and co-countable subsets of \((0,1)\). Since countable sets have Lebesgue measure \(0\), every set in \(\mathcal{G}\) has Lebesgue measure either \(0\) or \(1\).

For \(A\in\mathcal{G}\):

- If \(A\) is countable, then \(\lambda(A)=0\), so
  \[
  \int_A X\,d\lambda = 0.
  \]

- If \(A\) is co-countable, then \(A=(0,1)\setminus C\) for some countable \(C\), so
  \[
  \int_A X\,d\lambda
  =
  \int_{(0,1)} X\,d\lambda - \int_C X\,d\lambda
  =
  \int_0^1 \cos(\pi \omega)\,d\omega.
  \]

Compute the integral:

\[
\int_0^1 \cos(\pi \omega)\,d\omega
=
\left[\frac{\sin(\pi\omega)}{\pi}\right]_0^1
=
\frac{\sin\pi-\sin 0}{\pi}
=
0.
\]

Thus

\[
\int_A X\,d\lambda = 0
\qquad \text{for every } A\in\mathcal{G}.
\]

The constant function \(Z(\omega)=0\) is \(\mathcal{G}\)-measurable and satisfies the defining property of conditional expectation. Therefore,

\[
\mathbb{E}(X|\mathcal{G})=0 \quad \text{a.s.}
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
